steps.body: Things can be **heavy** or **light**. On a seesaw, the **heavier** side goes **down**.

widget.prompt: A rock and a feather sit on a seesaw. The rock's side goes down. Tap the heavier one.

hotspots.label: feather
hotspots.feedback: The feather's side went UP — up means lighter. The rock is heavier.

widget.missFeedback: The seesaw tells you — down side is heavier: the rock.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents heavier lighter.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for heavier lighter must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines heavier lighter.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Size can trick you! A big balloon is **lighter** than a small rock. Heavy is about weight, not size.

explanationVariants: Big does not mean heavy — a big balloon is full of air and lighter than a small rock.
Weight is not size: the small rock is heavier.

widget.prompt: A BIG balloon and a SMALL rock go on the seesaw. The rock's side goes down. Tap the heavier one.

hotspots.label: big balloon
hotspots.feedback: Its side went UP — the balloon is big but LIGHT. The rock is heavier.

widget.missFeedback: Size tricks you — the seesaw shows the small rock is heavier.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — down means heavier. Big does not mean heavy!

widget.prompt: A bucket and a cup. You pour the full cup into the bucket — lots of room is left. Tap the one that holds MORE.

hotspots.label: cup
hotspots.feedback: The cup emptied INTO the bucket with room to spare — the bucket holds more.

widget.missFeedback: Room was left over — the bucket holds more.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — the cup's water barely fills it: the bucket holds more.

explanationVariants: The up side of a seesaw is the lighter one.
Up means lighter; down means heavier.

widget.prompt: On a seesaw, the toy bear's side goes UP. What does that tell you?

options.label: The bear is heavier
options.feedback: Heavier goes DOWN — up means the bear is lighter.

options.label: The seesaw is broken
options.feedback: It is working — up simply means lighter.

options.label: The bear is bigger
options.feedback: The seesaw shows WEIGHT, not size — the bear is lighter.

explanationVariants: A spoon holds a tiny sip; a bowl holds lots — the spoon holds less.
Small container, small amount: the spoon.

widget.prompt: A soup bowl and a spoon. Tap the one that holds LESS.

hotspots.label: soup bowl
hotspots.feedback: The bowl holds MORE — the spoon holds less.

widget.missFeedback: A whole bowl fills many spoons — the spoon holds less.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — a spoon holds just a sip; the bowl holds much more.

explanationVariants: A level seesaw means the two sides weigh the same — equal weight.

widget.prompt: Put each seesaw clue in the right group.

items.label: two bags keep the seesaw level
items.feedback: Level means the weights are the same.

widget.missFeedback: Down means heavier, up means lighter, and level means the same.
widget.successFeedback: Right — the seesaw gives a clue about every weight.

hints: This seesaw is not tipping at all.
No tip means the weights are equal.

explanationVariants: Seesaw clues (a side going down or up) are about WEIGHT — heavier or lighter. Pouring clues (room left over or spilling over) are about HOLDING — more or less.
Two different properties give two different kinds of clues: a tipping seesaw always tells you about weight, while leftover room or an overflow always tells you about how much something holds.

widget.prompt: Some clues are about WEIGHT. Some are about how much something HOLDS. Sort each clue into the right group.

items.label: a dog's side of the seesaw goes down
items.feedback: Down on a seesaw means heavier — this is a WEIGHT clue.

items.label: a kitten's side of the seesaw goes up
items.feedback: Up on a seesaw means lighter — this is a WEIGHT clue.

items.label: an elephant toy's side of the seesaw goes down against a mouse toy
items.feedback: Down on a seesaw means heavier — the elephant toy is the heavier WEIGHT clue here.

items.label: a big block feels lighter than a tiny stone when you lift them
items.feedback: Big does not mean heavy — this WEIGHT clue says the block is the lighter one.

items.label: a pitcher still has water left after filling one small glass all the way
items.feedback: Water left over after filling the glass is a HOLDING clue — the pitcher holds more.

items.label: a teacup overflows before the teapot it is filled from is even half empty
items.feedback: Overflowing long before the teapot is empty is a HOLDING clue — the teacup holds less.

items.label: a small cup spills over before a big jug is even a quarter full
items.feedback: Spilling over so early is a HOLDING clue — the small cup holds less than the jug.

widget.missFeedback: First decide: is this clue about WEIGHT (a seesaw tipping) or about HOLDING (pouring, leftover room, or overflow)? Then pick the direction.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — sorted by both kinds of clue: weight clues into heavier or lighter, and holding clues into holds more or holds less.

hints: First ask: is this clue about weight, or about how much something holds?
A seesaw tipping down or up is always a weight clue.
Leftover room after pouring means holds more; spilling or overflowing early means holds less.

steps.body: Heavier goes down; lighter goes up; bigger containers hold more.
takeaways: Seesaw down = heavier; up = lighter; level = equal.
Big does not always mean heavy.
Buckets hold more than cups; spoons hold less than bowls.

concept.body: On a seesaw the heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. Level means equal.

explanationVariants: The book's side went down, so the book is heavier.

widget.prompt: A book and a sock on a seesaw. The book's side goes down. Which is heavier?

options.label: The sock
options.feedback: The sock floated UP — lighter. The book is heavier.

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Equal stays level — this tipped: the book is heavier.

options.label: Cannot tell
options.feedback: The seesaw told you — down side (book) is heavier.
